title: Completed algebraic and continuous formal conormal determinants with generic normalization
statement:
Let $k$ be a perfect field, $S$ a reduced finite-type $k$-algebra [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra], pure of dimension $d\geq0$ [def-weil-pure-dimension] and a local complete intersection over $k$ [def-weil-pbc-complete-intersection-over-field]. Let $\mathfrak m$ be a maximal ideal with residue field $k$, put $A=S_{\mathfrak m}$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime], and put $R=\widehat A$ [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion]. Assume $R$ reduced. Let $K_A$ be the stalk of the algebraic adjunction line of [lem-trf-flat-lci-canonical-adjunction]. Suppose a continuous local $k$-algebra surjection $T=k[[z_1,\ldots,z_n]]\twoheadrightarrow R$ [def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series] has kernel $J=(g_1,\ldots,g_c)$, where the $g_j$ form a regular sequence in $(z_1,\ldots,z_n)$ [def-weil-pbc-regular-sequence] and $n-c=d$.

Choose an algebraic local presentation $A=P/I$, with $P=k[u_1,\ldots,u_m]_{\mathfrak q}$ at a $k$-rational maximal ideal, and $I$ generated by a regular sequence of length $m-d$. Define the two-term conormal complexes in degrees $-1,0$ by
$$C_P=[I/I^2\xrightarrow{\mathrm d}\Omega^1_{P/k}\otimes_P A],\qquad C_T=[J/J^2\xrightarrow{\widehat{\mathrm d}}R^{\oplus n}],$$
where $\Omega$ is [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials] and $\widehat{\mathrm d}(h)=\sum_i(\partial h/\partial z_i)e_i$ uses termwise formal partial derivatives. Regard these as complexes of quasi-coherent modules on affine spectra in [def-pc-derived-category]; tensor extension is [def-weil-module-base-change]. A local lift $\alpha:P\to T$ of $P\to A\to R$ induces a chain map $C_P\otimes_A R\to C_T$: in degree $-1$ it sends $[h]\otimes1$ to $[\alpha(h)]$, and in degree $0$ it sends $\mathrm du_i\otimes1$ to $\widehat{\mathrm d}\alpha(u_i)$. Such lifts exist. These chain maps are quasi-isomorphisms and have the same class in the derived category for all lifts. On $H^0$ they identify both cokernels with $\Omega^1_{A/k}\otimes_A R$, sending $e_i$ to the continuous extension $\widehat d(z_i)$ of the universal derivation of $A$.

Their determinants [lem-trf-two-term-perfect-determinant] give a canonical isomorphism
$$\Phi_T:K_A\otimes_A R\xrightarrow{\sim}\lambda_T,\qquad\lambda_T=(\bigwedge^c_R J/J^2)^\vee\otimes_R\bigwedge^n_R R^{\oplus n},$$
where $\vee=\operatorname{Hom}_R(-,R)$. The construction respects algebraic presentation changes and continuous maps of regular power-series presentations inducing the identity of $R$; for any three presentations the induced comparisons compose. In particular this is a comparison of the completed algebraic line with the formal conormal determinant, not an application of base change of the base scheme.

The comparison has the following specified normalization. For every field $L$ and $k$-algebra map $\theta:R\to L$ whose restriction to $A$ factors through a generic point of $\operatorname{Spec}A$ in its smooth $d$-dimensional locus, put $M=\Omega^1_{A/k}\otimes_A L$. The base-changed formal conormal sequence is short exact and has cokernel $M$ via $e_i\mapsto\widehat d(z_i)\otimes1$. Let $\delta_T:\bigwedge^d_L M\to\lambda_T\otimes_R L$ be its determinant isomorphism: a wedge $v_1\wedge\cdots\wedge v_d$ is sent to
$$(\bar g_1\wedge\cdots\wedge\bar g_c)^\vee\otimes(\widehat{\mathrm d}g_1\wedge\cdots\wedge\widehat{\mathrm d}g_c\wedge\widetilde v_1\wedge\cdots\wedge\widetilde v_d),$$
with any lifts $\widetilde v_i\in L^n$. If $\gamma_A:K_A\otimes_A L\to\bigwedge^d_L M$ is the algebraic smooth-locus identification, then
$$\delta_T^{-1}\circ(\Phi_T\otimes_R L)=\gamma_A.$$
The same identity holds for every allowed formal presentation and every algebraic local presentation. No branch parametrization, meromorphic lattice or explicit residue fraction is asserted here.

from.place: Proof (1)--(2), semistable-alteration input in the nearby-cycle branch: ILO Exposé X, Theorem 3.4, Step 3, invoking Temkin 2010, Theorems 1.5 and 1.1 for a semistable multipointed modification. Temkin proof component: Marked dualizing line bundle and contracted-component degrees. Auxiliary input: Normalization and simple-pole branch calculation, prior to any numerical degree computation. Local input: The adjunction determinant calculation at a nodal point, before substituting f=xy and counting its branch poles. Missing prerequisite for this local input: compare the completed algebraic conormal determinant with an arbitrary regular formal presentation, preserving the generic differential map, before computing the plane residue.
